hypothesis: A disjoint native finite-CI model can include explicit 4f holes without adding and double counting the existing closed-core Sigma1; full Q-Q propagation can change the five-state differential response relative to bare P and diagonal-Q controls.
reference: Read-only v68_default Yb frozen common orbitals, Z=70, empirical Fermi nucleus A=175, Dirac-Coulomb only, ns=123; no orbital reoptimization
P: All [Xe]4f14 v1 configurations over v={6s1/2,5d3/2,5d5/2,6p1/2,6p3/2}, split into five J/parity sectors
Q: All [Xe]4f13 v2 configurations over precisely the same five valence orbitals, every allowed jj coupling tree in each sector; no amplitude pruning
excluded: 4f12 states, higher valence orbitals, other core holes, radial tails, Breit, QED, complete SD/CC and previously computed Sigma1; this is a model response probe, not a converged Yb spectrum
observables: Each bare/full-Q total energy, P weight, root shift, four ground-referenced transitions, two fine-structure splittings, full-Hamiltonian residual and independent dense eigenvector agreement; experimental residuals contextual only
zero: One native bare Hamiltonian for each N=69 sector from the same orbital pool and nucleus; no attachment threshold or separate ionic energy claimed
preflight: Record every CSF signature and sector/determinant count before constructing H. Reject any dimension/resource excess without changing configurations.
branch: Lowest P-connected root per fixed J/parity in a common pole-free interval containing its bare P energy; reject ambiguous/lost states or Q poles, never select by experimental agreement
stop: Failure in preflight, root identity, residual or dense anchor stops the probe; preserve failed outputs. Full-Q and diagonal-Q changes are alternatives, never additive corrections.
